RAJYA  SABHA
————
List of Questions for ORAL ANSWERS
to be asked at a sitting of the Rajya Sabha to be held on
Monday,  the November 19, 2007/Kartika 28, 1929 (Saka)
————
(Ministries: Earth Sciences; Food Processing Industries; Human Resource
Development; Law and Justice; Mines; Minority Affairs; New and Renewable
Energy; Power; Science and Technology; Social Justice and Empowerment;
Tribal Affairs; Women and Child Development)
Total number of questions — 20
Penalty in dowry death
cases
*41. SHRIMATI N.P. DURGA: Will
the Minister of LAW AND JUSTICE be
pleased to state:
(a) the reasons behind the Law
Commission's recommendation not to
prescribe capital punishment in dowry
death cases;
(b) whether the Commission's
recommendations are binding on
Government or are only persuasive in
nature; and
(c) what would be the legal position in
case the dowry death falls within the ambit
of offence of murder?
Policy for non-conventional energy
schemes
*42. SHRI M.V. MYSURA REDDY:
Will the Minister of NEW AND
RENEWABLE ENERGY be pleased to
state:
(a) whether Government have
formulated any non-conventional energy
policy in the country;
(b) if so, the details and the features
thereof and the role of such policy in rural,
tribal and remote areas of the country;
(c) whether this policy is being
implemented in the country;
(d) if so, the details of funds allocated,
released and actually spent on
implementation of various projects in rural
areas of the country during the last three
years, till date, project-wise, State-wise and
year-wise; and
(e) the details of non-conventional
energy sources which are operational at
present, alongwith the potential sources
for the same, State-wise?
Involvement of corporates for reforms
in higher education
*43. SHRIMATI PREMA
CARIAPPA:
SHRIMATI SHOBHANA
BHARTIA:
Will the Minister of HUMAN
RESOURCE DEVELOPMENT be
pleased to state:
(a) whether recently in the meeting
13

14
between the Prime Minister and the Union
Minister, a broad consensus has emerged
favouring involvement of corporates for
resource mobilization for reforms in higher
education;
(b) whether a campaign of Full Planning
Commission on Education for reforms in
institutions like UGC and AICTE took a
decisive shape in the month of September
and there was an overwhelming support
for adoption of Chinese models on the
expansion of higher education; and
(c) the steps being taken to improve
higher education in the country?
Loans to tribals in Jharkhand
*44. SHRI S.S. AHLUWALIA: Will the
Minister of TRIBAL AFFAIRS be pleased
to state:
(a) whether Government are seized of
the fact that the Scheduled Tribes people in
Jharkhand are denied loans by Commercial
Banks and Financial Institutions beyond a
term exceeding five years, even where such
loans are secured by borrowers, by
mortgaging their land properties;
(b) if so, the reasons for depriving
Scheduled Tribes in Jharkhand of the
benefit of long term loans against security;
(c) whether Government are
contemplating steps to amend the situation;
(d) if so, the details thereof; and
(e) if not, the reasons therefor?
Forest Rights Act
*45. SHRI SYED AZEEZ PASHA:
SHRI D. RAJA:
Will the Minister of TRIBAL AFFAIRS
be pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that even though
the Forest Rights Act was passed in 2006,
the rules have not been notified as yet; and
(b) if so, the details thereof and the
reasons therefor?
Target for additional power
generation
†*46. SHRI RAJ MOHINDER
SINGH MAJITHA:
DR. MURLI MANOHAR
JOSHI:
Will the Minister of POWER be pleased
to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that a target of
creating 10,159 Mega Watts power
generation capacity in the country for
2007-08 was fixed;
(b) if not, what was that target;
(c) whether it is also a fact that projects
related to creation of 2,645 MW power
generation capacity only were completed
from April to September, 2007; and
(d) if not, the facts in this regard?
Report on the development of
instrumentation
*47. SHRI HARISH RAWAT:
SHRI SANTOSH BAGRODIA:
Will the Minister of SCIENCE AND
TECHNOLOGY be pleased to state:
(a) the major recommendations of the
report prepared by the Indian National
Science Academy on development of
instrumentation in the country and
submitted to the Principal Scientific
Advisor; and
†Original notice of the question received in Hindi.

15
(b) the action taken by Government on
those recommendations?
Withdrawal of Life Support System
from terminally ill patients
*48. SHRI VIJAY J. DARDA:
SHRIMATI SHOBHANA
BHARTIA:
Will the Minister of LAW AND
JUSTICE be pleased to state:
(a) whether Law Commission's report
has recommended the setting up of a three-
member panel of reputed medical persons,
to clear the decision to withdraw Life
Support System from the terminally ill and
that patients and their relatives should
notify a High Court of the decision, so that
the doctor is immune from legal action;
(b) whether the Commission cited
several decisions of USA, Britain, Canada
and Australia and maintained that
withdrawal of Life Support System from
terminally ill patients has always been held
lawful in all the countries, while euthanasia
is and continues to be unlawful; and
(c) whether Government have accepted
and implemented the recommendation?
Working conditions of women
domestic helps
*49. SHRI RAJEEV
CHANDRASEKHAR: Will the Minister
of WOMEN AND CHILD
DEVELOPMENT be pleased to state:
(a) whether there is any proposal under
Government's consideration to lay down
rules governing the working conditions of
the women domestic helps, who are
generally exploited by their employers,
particularly in big cities; and
(b) if so, the details thereof and by when
they are likely to be implemented?
Projects under RGGVY in Andhra
Pradesh
*50. SHRI NANDI YELLAIAH: Will
the Minister of POWER be pleased to state:
(a) whether Andhra Pradesh
Government had sent proposals to cover
twenty-two districts under Rajiv Gandhi
Grameen Vidyutikaran Yojana (RGGVY),
at an estimated cost of Rs. 784.75 crore
and Rural Electrification Corporation
(REC) has, so far, sanctioned schemes for
only seventeen districts at a cost of
Rs. 648.20 crore;
(b) if so, by when schemes for remaining
five districts would be sanctioned by REC;
(c) whether actual release of funds from
REC is only Rs. 19.80 crore for covering
sanctioned schemes from four districts
only;
(d) if so, by when sanctioned funds for
approved schemes for remaining thirteen
districts would be released by REC; and
(e) the reasons for delay in releasing
funds for already sanctioned schemes?
Delay in pronouncing judgements
*51. SHRI VARINDER SINGH
BAJWA: Will the Minister of LAW AND
JUSTICE be pleased to state:
(a) whether Government have taken
note of the serious delays caused by the
the members of higher judiciary in the
country by sitting over orders for years
after having completed the hearings in the
matters;
(b) if so, whether Government proposes
to solve this problem through legislation or
directions and guidelines;
(c) if so, by when that is likely to be
done; and

16
(d) if not, how Government propose to
solve this problem?
New scheme for girl child
*52. SHRI T.T.V. DHINAKARAN:
Will the Minister of WOMEN AND
CHILD DEVELOPMENT be pleased to
state:
(a) whether a new scheme for the girl
child has been formulated;
(b) if so, the details thereof;
(c) whether funds for implementation
of the scheme would be allocated to States;
(d) if so, the details thereof; and
(e) if not, the reasons therefor?
Implementation of mega food projects
*53. SHRI KALRAJ MISHRA:
SHRI SANTOSH BAGRODIA:
Will the Minister of FOOD
PROCESSING INDUSTRIES be pleased
to state:
(a) whether many mega food projects
in the country are in the process of
implementation and if so, the details
thereof, State-wise; and
(b) how many more parks are proposed
to be established in Rajasthan?
Position of India in the Human
Development Index of UNDP
*54. SHRIMATI  SUPRIYA SULE:
SHRIMATI SHOBHANA
BHARTIA:
Will the Minister of HUMAN
RESOURCE DEVELOPMENT  be
pleased to state:
(a) is it correct that India still has the
largest number of illiterates in the world
and according to the 2001 census, India
had nearly 304 million illiterate people, aged
seven plus, and with its poor literacy level,
India ranks a poor  126th in the Human
Development Index of UNDP;
(b) whether despite two nation-wide
programmes, i.e. Sarva Shiksha Abhiyan
and the National Literacy Mission,
illiteracy rate has not been reduced; and
(c) if so, the main reasons for non-
elimination of  illiteracy completely in the
country?
Innovation in Science Pursuit for
Inspired Research Programme
*55. SHRI C. PERUMAL: Will the
Minister of SCIENCE AND
TECHNOLOGY be pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that Government
have planned to initiate Innovation in
Science Pursuit for Inspired Research
Programme for the promotion of research
activities;
(b) if so, the details thereof;
(c) the fiscal allocation for this
programme; and
(d) the number of scientists and research
scholars expected to be selected under this
programme, State-wise?
Cases of ragging
*56. SHRI MAHMOOD A.
MADANI:
SHRI SANTOSH BAGRODIA:
Will the Minister of HUMAN
RESOURCE DEVELOPMENT be
pleased to state:
(a) the number and details of cases of
ragging reported during the last three
academic years, State-wise and year-wise;
(b) whether Government plan to

17
introduce better methods of introducing
freshers to the old students; and
(c) if so, the details thereof?
Malnutrition and infant mortality
†*57. SHRI PYARELAL
KHANDELWAL: Will the Minister of
WOMEN AND CHILD
DEVELOPMENT be pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that the cases of
malnutrition and infant mortality in the
country are constantly on rise;
(b) if so, the details thereof, State-wise;
and
(c) the details of the efforts being made
by Government to prevent and control the
situation, and the achievements made in
that regard?
Establishment of Central university
†*58 SHRI MANGANI LAL
MANDAL: Will the Minister of HUMAN
RESOURCE DEVELOPMENT be
pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that in order to
create interest in the students in respect of
higher education in the country and to make
norms-based higher education world class,
the Knowledge Commission has
recommended to set up about 1500 Central
universities in the country; and
(b) if so, the details regarding the
progress made in this regard so far?
Power projects in Vidarbha
†*59. SHRI DATTA MEGHE: Will the
Minister of POWER be pleased to state:
(a) the names of power projects being
built by Government, keeping in view
shortage of electricity in the Vidarbha region
of Maharashtra;
(b) the number of such power projects
out of the above, construction work of
which is going to be completed within a
year;
(c) the power projects where the
construction work is getting delayed and
the reasons for the delays; and
(d) the steps being taken to speed up
the construction work of power projects,
keeping in view the backwardness and the
acute electricity problem in this area?
Goals to achieve literacy
*60. SHRI RA VULA CHANDRA
SEKAR REDDY: W ill the Minister of
HUMAN RESOURCE DEVELOPMENT
be pleased to state:
(a) details regarding the goals set to
achieve literacy in the country especially
in Andhra Pradesh during the last three
years, year-wise; and
(b) the present position thereof in that
State?
†Original notice of the question received in Hindi.

RAJYA SABHA
————
List of Questions for  WRITTEN ANSWERS
to be asked at a sitting of the Rajya Sabha to be held on
Monday, the November 19, 2007/Kartika 28, 1929 (Saka)
————
(Ministries: Earth Sciences; Food Processing Industries; Human Resource
Development; Law and Justice; Mines; Minority Affairs; New and Renewable
Energy; Power; Science and Technology; Social Justice and Empowerment;
Tribal Affairs; Women and Child Development)
Total number of questions — 79
Electronic measurement of
earthquakes
87. SHRI JAI PARKASH
AGGARWAL: W ill the Minister of
EARTH SCIENCES be pleased to state:
(a) whether Government have
formulated any scheme to set up electronic
system for accurate measurement of
intensity of earthquakes, in the wake of
severe earthquake of October, 2005;
(b) if so, the details thereof;
(c) by when this system is proposed to
be set up; and
(d) whether it would find out the
earthquakes from the atmospheric and
ocean current?
Instruments/computers for weather
forecasting
88. SHRI ABU ASIM AZMI: Will the
Minister of EARTH SCIENCES be pleased
to state:
(a) whether the instruments/computers
available for weather forecasting, ocean
information and tropical meteorology are
completely out-dated;
(b) if so, whether Government are
planning to buy/produce super computers
for tracking changes in the climate of the
country;
(c) if so, the details thereof; and
(d) the funds allocated for the purpose?
Shortage of food processing units in
Rajasthan
89. SHRI HARISH RAWAT:
SHRI SANTOSH BAGRODIA:
Will the Minister of FOOD
PROCESSING INDUSTRIES be pleased
to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that there is acute
shortage of food processing units in
Rajasthan; and
(b) if so, the incentives Government
plan to give for setting up more such units
in that State?
Grants for food processing industries
in Sikkim
90. SHRI O.T. LEPCHA: Will the
Minister of FOOD PROCESSING
INDUSTRIES be pleased to state:
(a) the details of financial assistance
granted for setting up of food processing

24
industries in the country under various
schemes, particularly in Sikkim; and
(b) the details of amount spent on
setting up of food processing industries in
the country during the last three years,
State-wise?
Objectives of SSA
91. SHRI JAI PARKASH
AGGARWAL: W ill the Minister of
HUMAN RESOURCE DEVELOPMENT
be pleased to state:
(a) the objectives of the Sarva Shiksha
Abhiyan;
(b) whether these objectives have been
achieved;
(c) if not, how much time has lapsed
between the target dates and today;
(d) the reasons for failure in
achievement of targets;
(e) what percentage of the child
population remains out of school on this
day;
(f) by when these children would be
brought under the Sarva Shiksha Abhiyan
Programme;
(g) what steps are being taken to
accelerate the achievement of targets; and
(h) what percentage of funds is being
utilized to achieve these targets?
Setting up of new universities
92. MS. PRAMILA BOHIDAR:
SHRI B.J. PANDA:
 Will the Minister of HUMAN
RESOURCE DEVELOPMENT be
pleased to state:
(a) whether it is proposed to set up 30
new universities for expanding access to
higher education in the country;
(b) if so, the details thereof, indicating
the universities that would be set up in
Orissa;
(c) whether it is also proposed to set up
6,000 quality schools, one in each block
of the country, to secure excellence in
public schooling; and
(d) if so, the details thereof, indicating
inter-alia, those that are proposed to be set
up in Orissa?
Education in the National Common
Minimum Programme
93. SHRI ABU ASIM AZMI:  Will the
Minister of HUMAN RESOURCE
DEVELOPMENT be pleased to state:
(a) the details of steps initiated by
Government  to fulfil the promises made
in the National Common Minimum
Programme in regard to education;
(b) whether the Right to Education,
enshrined in the Constitution, has been
fulfilled;
(c) if not, the reasons therefor; and
(d) the steps taken to provide free and
compulsory education to children?
Expenditure on education
94. SHRI GIREESH KUMAR
SANGHI:
SHRI SANTOSH BAGRODIA:
 Will the Minister of HUMAN
RESOURCE DEVELOPMENT be
pleased to state:
(a) what is the percentage of GDP
towards higher education, primary and
middle education during the last three
years;
(b) how it compares with the developed
countries; and

25
(c) whether Government plan to
increase this in the coming years?
High illiteracy rate States
95. SHRIMATI SUPRIYA SULE:  Will
the Minister of HUMAN RESOURCE
DEVELOPMENT be pleased to state:
(a) whether eight States alone account
for nearly 70 per cent of the country's
illiterates; which means that out of 304
million illiterate people in the country,
212.19 million come from these eight
States alone;
(b) whether, according to the recently
released reports on the status of adult
literacy in the country, 13 States need to
pay special attention for raising their
literacy levels;
(c) if so, whether this report was
brought out by the National Literacy
Mission; and
(d) if so, what concrete steps and
measures Government propose to take, to
help and assist these States to improve the
position?
Impact of price rise on Mid-Day Meal
Scheme
96. SHRI RAJKUMAR DHOOT:  Will
the Minister of HUMAN RESOURCE
DEVELOPMENT be pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that Mid-Day
Meal Scheme of Government will get a jolt
as the Department of Food and Public
Distribution has enhanced the prices of
wheat and rice for the Scheme, and that
for expansion of the scheme, the prices will
be still higher;
(b) if so, the details thereof;
(c) whether Government are
considering any alternative proposal for
this highly successful project;
(d) if so, the details thereof; and
(e) if not, the steps being taken to make
this project a success?
Gender parity in higher education
97. SHRI RAJKUMAR DHOOT:  Will
the Minister of HUMAN RESOURCE
DEVELOPMENT be pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that as per the
mid term review of UN Millennium
Development Goals 2015, while gender
parity is on track for primary and secondary
education, the progress is slow in higher
education;
(b) if so, the details thereof; and
(c) the steps being taken for gender
parity in higher education by the stipulated
time-frame?
Components of SSA
98. SHRIMATI N.P. DURGA: Will the
Minister of HUMAN RESOURCE
DEVELOPMENT be pleased to state:
(a) the details of components under the
SSA;
(b) the targets set under SSA during the
last three years; year-wise and State-wise;
(c) the achievements of targets set
during the last three years; year-wise and
State-wise;
(d) whether it is a fact that enrolment
targets under SSA have not been achieved;
and
(e) if so, the reasons therefor?
Extension Centres of IITs
99. SHRIMATI N.P. DURGA: Will the
Minister of HUMAN RESOURCE
DEVELOPMENT be pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that Government

26
†Original notice of the question received in Hindi.
are planning to set up extension centres of
the existing IITs outside their main
campuses;
(b) if so, whether any State has
requested for setting up of such extension
centres; and
(c) if so, the details thereof?
Amount for development of  languages
100. SHRI O.T. LEPCHA: Will the
Minister of HUMAN RESOURCE
DEVELOPMENT be pleased to state:
(a) the total amount allocated for
development of various languages,
including Lepcha language, during the last
three years, year-wise; and
(b) the total amount actually spent on
the development of various languages in
the country during this period, language-
wise/year-wise?
Kendriya Vidyalayas in Sikkim
101. SHRI O.T. LEPCHA: Will the
Minister of HUMAN RESOURCE
DEVELOPMENT be pleased to state:
(a) whether Government have a
proposal to set up new Kendriya
Vidyalayas in the country, especially in
Sikkim, during the current financial year;
and
(b) if so, the location-wise and State-
wise details thereof, where these schools
are planned to be set up and by when?
Commission for higher education
†102. SHRI KESHUBHAI S. PATEL:
Will the Minister of HUMAN
RESOURCE DEVELOPMENT be
pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that Government
are considering to constitute any
commission for getting better results in
higher education;
(b) if so, whether Government have
taken any steps in this regard; and
(c) if so, the details thereof and if not,
the reasons therefor?
Central university status to Garhwal
and Kumaon universities
†103. SHRI HARISH RAWAT: Will the
Minister of HUMAN RESOURCE
DEVELOPMENT be pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that Central
university status have been given to the
universities in all the States of the North-
East, having special status; and
(b) if so, whether his Ministry is
considering the proposal to give Central
university status to the Garhwal and
Kumaon universities of Uttarakhand, as
these universities are also situated in a State
having special status?
Sexual abuse in Delhi University
104. SHRI VARINDER SINGH
BAJWA: Will the Minister of HUMAN
RESOURCE DEVELOPMENT be
pleased to state:
(a) the number of cases of sexual abuse
by members of teaching fraternity in the
University of Delhi and in the colleges
affiliated to it that have come to notice and
have been investigated or are being
investigated by the Committees constituted
for the purpose;
(b) whether it is a fact that action on
the recommendations of the Committees
is being delayed by the Vice-Chancellor;
(c) if so, whether Government propose
to issue suitable directions so as to ensure

27
that no undue delays are caused in such
cases; and
(d) the details of the recent cases
disposed of or being investigated, case-
wise?
Regional Language Centres
†105. SHRI SAMAN PATHAK: Will
the Minister of HUMAN RESOURCE
DEVELOPMENT be pleased to state:
(a) the number of Regional Language
Centres (RLC) set up for the development
of recognized languages in the country;
(b) whether Government are
considering to set up more new Regional
Language Centres; and
(c) whether Government are having any
proposal for setting up a branch of Regional
Language Centre in Darjeeling, for the
development of Nepali language?
Changing educational expenditure
from students
†106. SHRI DATTA MEGHE: Will the
Minister of HUMAN RESOURCE
DEVELOPMENT be pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that the Central
Advisory Board of Education has made this
recommendation that 20 per cent of total
expenditure on education may be charged
from students;
(b) if so, whether Government have not
accepted this recommendation;
(c) whether it is also a fact that a need
is being felt to bring changes with regard
to the tuition fees in universities and
colleges in several States; and
(d) if so, the decision taken by
Government in this regard?
New IITs and IIMs
107. MS. PRAMILA BOHIDAR:
SHRI B. J. PANDA:
Will the Minister of HUMAN
RESOURCE DEVELOPMENT be
pleased to state:
(a) whether it is proposed to set up eight
new IITs and seven new IIMs in the
country;
(b) if so, the details thereof, indicating
whether any such institute would be set up
in Orissa also; and
(c) if so, the details thereof?
Dismal standard of Indian graduates
108. SHRI RAMDAS AGARWAL:
Will the Minister of HUMAN
RESOURCE DEVELOPMENT be
pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that higher
education in the country is in a dismal state,
as only nine per cent of Indian graduates
are employed, while 50 per cent of the
students do not have any understanding of
the course they are studying;
(b) whether HRD Minister, at the
Conference of Vice-Chancellors, admitted
that higher education in India is a sick child
and it is time to bring in the necessary
changes; and
(c) if so, what were the
recommendations made at the above
mentioned conference and what action
Government have taken thereon?
†Original notice of the question received in Hindi.

28
Obstacles in universalization of
elementary education
109. SHRIMATI SHOBHANA
BHARTIA:
SHRIMATI  SUPRIYA SULE:
Will the Minister of HUMAN
RESOURCE DEVELOPMENT be
pleased to state:
(a) whether the path leading towards
universalizing elementary education in the
country is fraught with obstacles with
States and Union Territory expressing their
strong reservations towards the model
Right to Education Bill, 2006; if so,
whether  Prime Minister has decided to set
up a high-level Group to examine the legal,
constitutional and financial implications of
the Right to Education;
(b) whether the Group has already given
its recommendations to Government;
(c) if so, the details thereof; and
(d) by when a final decision in this
regard is likely to be taken?
Kendriya Vidyalayas without
permanent land
110. SHRIMATI SUPRIYA SULE:
Will the Minister of HUMAN
RESOURCE DEVELOPMENT be
pleased to state:
(a) whether about 38 Kendriya
Vidyalayas (KV) scattered in different parts
of the country are without permanent land;
(b) if so, whether Parliamentary
Standing Committee on Human Resource
Development had identified 38 Kendriya
Vidyalayas where land has not been made
available by the sponsoring agencies even
after a lapse of 20-25 years in some cases;
(c) if so, in which States these Kendriya
Vidyalayas are set up; and
(d) by when a final decision to provide
all infrastructural facilities to these
Kendriya Vidyalayas would be considered?
Availability of study materials on the
Internet
†111. SHRI MANOHAR JOSHI: Will
the Minister of HUMAN RESOURCE
DEVELOPMENT be pleased to state:
(a) whether Government are
considering  to make available all types of
books of higher education and important
research documents on various subjects
and journals on the Internet, so that
students and teachers could download any
of these contents as per their requirement,
on payment of nominal charges;
(b) whether in view of this, any plan is
under consideration of Government to
provide computers to the colleges on half
price; and
(c) whether any plan for providing free
broad-band connection at the residence of
the teachers is under consideration in the
University Grants Commission?
Implementation of e-courts project
112. SHRI B.J. PANDA:
MS. PRAMILA BOHIDAR:
Will the Minister of LAW AND
JUSTICE be pleased to state:
(a) what is the status of implementation
of e-courts project in the country;
(b) whether it would inter link all the
courts across the country and help the
litigants to have access to authorized
documents; and
(c) the details of the districts where it is
proposed to be implemented in the first
phase and the time-frame within which all
the districts in Orissa would be covered
under this project?
†Original notice of the question received in Hindi.

29
Electoral rolls with voters'
